Bond + nominate up to 16 validators, OR: Bond + nominate up to 16 validators, OR join a nomination pool.
Calls `0x1::delegation_pool::add_stake`: Calls `0x1::delegation_pool::add_stake` against a pool address. Stake activates at the next epoch. Unlock moves it to a pending-inactive bucket; after the lockup cycle (typically 30 days) it becomes withdrawable.
Delegate to a vote account; rewards each: Delegate to a vote account; rewards each epoch (~2 days).
Each stake position is its own on-chain: Each stake position is its own on-chain stake account: a fresh keypair initialized with `StakeProgram` and delegated to a vote account. Rewards land at every epoch boundary.
Each validator runs its own staking-pool: Each validator runs its own staking-pool contract; staking calls `deposit_and_stake` with NEAR attached. Unstake places funds into a pending bucket; after 4 epochs (~52h) they're withdrawable via `withdraw`.
Lock ICP into a neuron; rewards scale wi: Lock ICP into a neuron; rewards scale with dissolve delay.
Move call `request_add_stake` to a valid: Move call `request_add_stake` to a validator; epoch ~24h.
Staking creates a `StakedSui` object own: Staking creates a `StakedSui` object owned by your wallet. To unstake, the same object is passed to `request_withdraw_stake`; principal + rewards return at the next epoch boundary.
Staking on ICP means creating an NNS neu: Staking on ICP means creating an NNS neuron with a chosen dissolve delay (≥ 6 months for rewards eligibility, up to 8 years for max maturity bonus). Voting on proposals — directly or via followees — drives the reward rate.
Two paths: direct nomination (`staking::: Two paths: direct nomination (`staking::bond` + `staking::nominate`, requires the chain's active minimum bond, currently ~250 DOT) or nomination pools (`nomination_pools::join`, no minimum, recommended for smaller stakers).

settings.aboutSubtitle: A self-custodial multi-chain wallet focused on local control, transparent network access, and minimal trust assumptions.
settings.aboutEthosLines:
Free and open source.
No data collected.
Decentralized software.
We don't have servers to process your data.
Self-custodial.
You are in charge of your own keys.
settings.aboutNarrativeParagraphs:
Your wallet data stays on your device unless you explicitly choose to share it. Spectra is designed so key material, watched addresses, and local transaction state remain under your control.

You keep control over recovery phrases and private keys at all times. The app is a client, not a custodian, and it should be understood as local wallet software that talks to chain infrastructure rather than a hosted account platform.
settings.buyProvidersIntro: Two ways to turn cash into crypto. Availability, fees, identity checks, supported networks and regional coverage differ by provider — check before you pay.
settings.buyOnrampNote: On-ramps send what you buy straight to a wallet address you enter, so the coins arrive in Spectra without a second step.
settings.buyExchangeNote: Exchanges hold what you buy in an account of theirs. To hold it yourself, withdraw to one of your Spectra addresses afterwards.
settings.buyListingNote: Listed alphabetically. Spectra is not affiliated with any of them and does not receive a fee.
settings.buyWarning: Spectra does not process purchases. Always double-check the wallet address, selected chain, and asset before paying, because crypto transfers are typically irreversible.
Pinned assets stay in the Assets list ev: Pinned assets stay in the Assets list even when their balance is zero.
